absent: Definitions and contracts of diagnostic helpers that stage prefix output, emit blank separators and lines, test and invoke optional scheduler dump hooks, and format CPU arguments are not shown.

Full layouts of scheduler, per CPU, runqueue extension, dispatch queue, task extension, dump context and data, event statistics, capability mask, and exit info objects beyond fields observed during dumping and balancing.

Numeric values and bit positions of scheduler capability indices, runqueue flags, task state and operation state masks and shifts, slice defaults, bypass balancing thresholds and percentages, and dump buffer sizes.

Locking and lifetime rules for event counters, performance shard capability masks, exit info, stall masks, kobject release, and scheduler root pointer beyond the RCU preempt and runqueue guards observed.

Behavior of bypass queue selection, remote run permission, abbreviated dequeue and nested enqueue, runqueue lock dropping, CPU rescheduling, tracing, timer management, and NUMA node iteration helpers.
Enable state transitions, root installation and removal, exit claim and formatting, exit reason mapping, and asynchronous disable work scheduling beyond the gating checks shown.
Scheduler attribute operations and events show routines, default groups, sysfs operations, kset handling, and container conversions beyond the capabilities show and uevent filtering shown.
Stack trace capture and rendering, time conversion and monotonic clock source, bitmap conversion, allocation failure paths beyond the single out of memory return, and warning reporting semantics.

findings.text: Externally visible rescue dump helper summarizes runqueue rescue state for diagnostics, while builds without sub scheduler support substitute an empty inline with identical signature that produces no output.
RCU stall detector and soft plus hard lockup notifiers are externally reachable hooks that request scheduler shutdown with an error exit when the extended scheduler is active.
Bypass dispatch disable helper is externally reachable and releases a prior bypass dispatch claim together with its enable depth accounting.
Capability attribute show routine serves as sysfs read entry that renders one line per capability with its aggregated CPU set, reporting allocation failure as out of memory.
Uevent routine serves as kobject uevent entry that annotates scheduler objects with their scheduler name while silently ignoring other kobject types encountered during parent chain traversal.
Bypass load balance timer routine serves as timer expiry entry that balances bypass queues across NUMA nodes and conditionally re arms itself.

Diagnostic dump session state comprises an output stream reference, a reusable line buffer with fill cursor, a first output marker, a line prefix, and a CPU marker that is invalidated when the session ends.

CPU diagnostic view spans runqueue scheduling counters and flags, release and kick synchronization state, current task identity and class, runnable list membership, synchronization mask, and per CPU kick preempt and wait sets.

Task diagnostic view spans scheduler association and level, dispatch queue association and flags, operation state and sequence, runnable timestamp, state and flag word, sticky and holding CPUs, virtual time slice and weight, allowed CPUs, and migration disabled state.
Rescue state comprises a dispatch queue occupancy count, a remaining time budget, and an optional current rescued task with name and identifier.

Scheduler object as observed here carries a per CPU area, performance shard table with capability masks, bypass depth slice timestamp claim and enable depths plus load balance timer and masks, exit info and stall mask with disable work, kobject with type and attributes, and operations name with sub cgroup identity and level.

Sysfs registration comprises an attribute list holding scheduler operations and events entries with optional capabilities entry, a kobject type binding release operation sysfs operations and default groups, and a kset uevent operations table binding the uevent routine.

Diagnostic flush has no effect when no bytes are pending, otherwise it guarantees that the first emitted content is preceded by a distinguishing blank line and that every emitted segment carries the session prefix and line termination even when the staging buffer overflowed without a terminator.

CPU diagnostic output is suppressed for idle runqueues lacking scheduler hook output, where idle means empty runnable list with idle class current, while non idle runqueues always emit their standard summary.

CPU standard summary plus optional scheduler hook output is staged in a nested buffer so commitment to the outer stream occurs only when warranted, with outer overflow state preserved and inner overflow propagated without committing when the outer stream was already full.

Task lines distinguish scheduler ownership with a marker and identify the owning scheduler as root at level zero or as sub level plus cgroup identity otherwise, alongside elapsed time since becoming runnable and dispatch queue identity or an unavailable sentinel when unassociated.

Task numeric state separates the packed state and flag word into state value and remaining flags, separates packed operation state into state and sequence components, and reports sticky and holding CPUs plus virtual time slice weight allowed CPUs and migration disabled state.
Rescue summary reports queue length and budget expressed in microseconds together with rescued task name and identifier, using none and negative one when no task is being rescued.

Event statistics reporting starts from zeroed totals and accumulates each per CPU counter across all possible CPUs with single read semantics per counter, covering exactly the event family enumerated for this subsystem.

Capability display aggregates each capability across all performance shards by reframing a temporary mask to each shard range and merging with logical or, then converts the internal word layout to bitmap layout for human readable mask rendering.
Scheduler sysfs attribute set always exposes operations and events and additionally exposes capabilities only when sub scheduler support is compiled in, with null termination.
Uevent handling accepts only objects whose type matches the scheduler kobject type and ignores kset objects to avoid misinterpreting unrelated kobjects during hierarchy traversal.
Lockup and stall initiated shutdown requests are honored only while a root scheduler exists and its enable state is enabling or enabled, otherwise they report no action.

RCU stall handling derives an exit CPU from the stalled set with negative one for empty sets, claims error exit at most once, records message kind reason CPU and mask, captures a stack trace when available, and schedules asynchronous disable work.

Bypass per CPU balancing acts only when donor surplus exceeds a threshold derived from balance interval and bypass slice, moves only tasks still owned by the donor runqueue with an eligible donee and remote run permission, and stops once donor target is reached or no donees remain.

Node level bypass balancing computes a fair per CPU target and a higher donor limit, treats under target online CPUs in the node as receivers, drives over limit non receivers as donors, wakes receivers that gained tasks, and emits a trace with task counts balance total and before after spread.
Bypass balance timer does nothing unless bypass dispatch is enabled, otherwise it balances every node containing CPUs and re arms only when a non zero interval is configured.

Bypass depth accounting treats transitions between zero and one as activation edges that install or restore the default slice and record activation and duration events with a monotonic timestamp, while nested levels only adjust the counter.

Bypass dispatch enablement is single claim guarded and increments enable depth on both the requesting scheduler and its bypass host, starting the host timer when needed, with disable symmetrically clearing the claim and decrementing the same depths.
Idle renotification for root schedulers sets a root specific runqueue flag, while non root schedulers set a per CPU renotify marker plus a sub scheduler specific runqueue flag.

CPU diagnostic inspection holds the target runqueue lock with interrupts saved across idle determination, staged summary generation, optional scheduler hook invocation, commit decision, and task list traversal, releasing exactly once on every path including early skips.

Bypass task movement holds the donor runqueue lock with interrupts disabled plus the donor dispatch queue lock, inserts a cursor to allow safe iteration, temporarily drops both locks at batch boundaries to reduce hold time, then reacquires and resumes, finally removing the cursor before release.
Bypass depth increments and decrements require the bypass mutex to be held by the caller, as enforced by lock ownership assertions, and perform counter updates with single write semantics.
Root scheduler lookup for lockup and stall paths is protected by RCU read side guard, with stall exit claiming and exit info mutation additionally protected by a preempt disable guard.

Diagnostic session lifecycle starts with first output pending and empty cursor, accumulates hook output, emits with prefix on flush while clearing first and cursor, and ends invalidated so further flushes are inert until reinitialized.

Bypass depth counter lifecycle rests at zero when inactive, moves to one on outermost activation to install bypass timing, remains above one under nesting without side effects, and returns to zero on outermost exit to restore normal timing and account duration.
Scheduler enable lifecycle gates external fault handling so enabling and enabled permit error exit initiation while all other enable states reject lockup and stall requests without side effects.

Bypass dispatch claim lifecycle rests unclaimed, transitions to claimed on first enable with host depth bumps and timer start, ignores duplicate enables, and returns to unclaimed on disable with matching depth drops.

Committing staged CPU output without checking outer available space risks a fault when the outer stream already overflowed, so commitment must be skipped in that case while still propagating inner overflow status.

Staged hook output may contain multiple embedded lines or lack final termination after overflow, so flushing must segment on both newline and terminator and always emit termination to avoid merging or truncating diagnostic lines.

Bypass movement must verify continued donor runqueue ownership before migration because earlier placements can leave tasks linked to another runqueue, and nested dispatch queue locking is safe only because this balancer is the sole mover between bypass queues.

Incorrect bypass accounting such as negative depth, decrement below one, duplicate dispatch claim, or non positive enable depth indicates logic error and is reported via one time warnings without correcting the underlying state beyond the attempted update.

Capability display allocates temporary aggregation storage and must fail cleanly on allocation failure, while task and stall stack capture is only available when stack trace support is compiled in and must be skipped otherwise.

Uevent dispatch reaches both scheduler kobjects and parent kset kobjects, so failure to check kobject type before container conversion would corrupt memory by misinterpreting a kset object as a scheduler.
Capability indices map to human readable names enq_immed and enq and preempt and perf in index order.
Scheduler uevent payload uses variable name SCXOPS carrying the scheduler operations name.
Event identifiers include SCX_EV_SELECT_CPU_FALLBACK, SCX_EV_DISPATCH_LOCAL_DSQ_OFFLINE, SCX_EV_DISPATCH_KEEP_LAST, SCX_EV_ENQ_SKIP_EXITING, SCX_EV_ENQ_SKIP_MIGRATION_DISABLED, SCX_EV_REENQ_IMMED.
Event identifiers include SCX_EV_REENQ_REPEAT, SCX_EV_REFILL_SLICE_DFL, SCX_EV_SLICE_CLAMPED, SCX_EV_SLICE_DENIED, SCX_EV_BYPASS_DURATION.
Event identifiers include SCX_EV_BYPASS_DISPATCH, SCX_EV_BYPASS_ACTIVATE, SCX_EV_INSERT_NOT_OWNED, SCX_EV_SUB_BYPASS_DISPATCH, SCX_EV_SUB_FORCED_ADMIT.
Event identifiers include SCX_EV_SUB_PREEMPT_DENIED, SCX_EV_SUB_KICK_DENIED, SCX_EV_SUB_REENQ_DENIED, SCX_EV_SUB_CIDPERF_DENIED, SCX_EV_SUB_RESCUE.

Sentinels observed are negative one for dump CPU invalidation and for exit CPU when no CPU stalled and for rescued task identifier when none, plus unavailable text marker for dispatch queue identity and bit zero for bypass dispatch claim.
